description: Official NIST ACVP vectors for ML-DSA-65 keyGen. This is the EXTERNAL ANCHOR for the post-quantum half — the only group whose authority does not come from this project. Only the public key is compared; NIST's `sk` is the expanded 4032-byte form, while this standard keeps secret keys as a 32-byte seed. See FORMAT.md.

provenance.copyright: A work of the U.S. government — in the public domain.

notes: Only the PUBLIC KEY is compared. NIST also supplies `sk` (4032 bytes), but that is the EXPANDED key; this project keeps secret keys as a 32-byte seed, and there is no bridge between the two.
NIST's seed is placed in the ML-DSA HALF of the hybrid secret key; the Ed25519 half is irrelevant to this comparison.

fips204_interface.method: Run NIST's sigVer vectors through this implementation: the `external` group matched 1/1 while the `internal` group disagreed on 3 of 15, and only on cases NIST marks as passing. That is the signature of one side using the external interface.
fips204_interface.why_it_matters: FIPS 204 defines TWO interfaces. The external one computes M' = 0x00 || len(ctx) || ctx || M and signs that; the internal one signs M directly. Choose the wrong one and both sides are "FIPS 204 compliant" while neither can verify the other. TCC uses EXTERNAL with an EMPTY context.

sig_ver.description: NIST sigVer vectors. ONLY the cases with an empty `context` are usable — this implementation does not support a non-empty context.
sig_ver.limitations: The `sigGen` group is UNUSABLE: ACVP supplies secret keys in the EXPANDED 4032-byte form, while the `ml-dsa` library loads only a 32-byte seed. There is no bridge, which is why the signing direction is anchored by cross-checking against dilithium-py instead.
